## Design

### 2026-10-06 — I set up the project for OutBound and started making the schematic design in KiCad 10. Beacause Waveshare doesn't have a  KiCad symbol file for the ESP32-S3-A7670E-4G board on their wiki, I built a cu

**3h**

I set up the project for OutBound and started making the schematic design in KiCad 10. Beacause Waveshare doesn't have a  KiCad symbol file for the ESP32-S3-A7670E-4G board on their wiki, I built a custom 20-pin symbol from scratch inside the KiCad Symbol Editor.

What I Accomplished:
1.Custom Board Symbol:Designed and saved the `ESP32-S3-A7670E-4G` symbol with proper electrical pin types (3.3V,GND, 5V, display SPI, LED matrix output, encoder inputs, and button inputs).
2.Schematic Layout: Placed the board (U1), two rotary encoders (SW1  for the front turntable, SW2  for side volume), and two 12mm tactile push buttons (SW3 and SW4) onto the canvas.
3.KiCad Workflow:Learned how KiCad pin connection points, wire stubs, and Net Label routing work to keep complex schematics clean.

Next stuff left to do:
Attach Net Labels to all peripheral lines, add power/ground symbols, and assign physical footprints  before moving to PCB layout.

### 2026-10-07 — I. System Overview & :

**10h**

I. System Overview & :
 Custom Tier 2 Hack Club OutBound distraction-free handheld hardware device ($65 budget target).

1.Architecture: 2 board sandwich consisting of two identical 9.2 cm × 6.7 cm PCBs (Board A and Board B) mounted face to face.

2.Interconnect Gap: 15 mm internal space maintained by four corner M2.5/M3 brass hex standoffs.

3.Board Thickness: Standard 1.6 mm FR4 per PCB (3.2 mm total PCB thickness).

4.Dimension: 9.2 cm (W) × 6.7 cm (H) × 18.2 mm (D) (~1.82 cm overall thickness).

5.Interconnect Strategy: Internal 2.54 mm pitch pin headers passing power rails, display/LED buses, control lines, and 2 dedicated amplified audio pins.

II. Physical Board Layering & Component Placement

1.Board A serves as the primary user interface plate. Its front outer face features a centered ILI9341 2.4-inch TFT LCD screen for the main graphical user interface, flanked by a MAX7219 20 mm 8x8 LED matrix for retro animations and status indicators, an EC11 low-profile rotary encoder jog wheel for UI navigation, and three 6x6 mm micro tactile push buttons mapped to primary system controls (Left/Brake, Right/Gas, and Home). On its rear inner face, facing into the internal gap, an 8-ohm 1W enclosed cavity micro-speaker is mounted flat against the PCB back, accompanied by an edge-mounted B103 volume thumbwheel extending 0.5 cm past the board boundary for external adjustment, along with solder pads for the interconnect header that receives power, speaker signals, and display buses.

2.Board B houses the compute, audio, and power infrastructure. Its front inner face contains a flat 1200–1500 mAh LiPo battery (3.4 cm × 5.0 cm × 0.8 cm) secured with protective foam backing, an MH-CD42 charge/boost module positioned with its USB-C port flush against the outer board edge for side charging access, a MAX98357A I2S amplifier placed directly adjacent to the ESP32-S3 audio output pins to minimize digital trace length, and an SS-12D00G5 SPDT slide switch placed along the perimeter so its toggle lever extends into the side gap. The rear outer face acts as the exposed cyberdeck core, mounting the Waveshare ESP32-S3-A7670E-4G development module with accessible debug USB-C and tactile reset/boot buttons, a 5MP camera lens cutout positioned away from user hand grip zones, and four M2.5/M3 corner mounting holes.

III.Power Circuitry & Signal Routing
Power distribution is handled entirely through internal PCB copper traces without loose wiring harnesses. The positive terminal of the 3.7V LiPo battery routes directly through the SS-12D00G5 mini slide switch before reaching the MH-CD42 charge and boost module. Toggling the switch to the ON position connects the battery to the module input to generate the stable 5V power rail for the microcontroller, audio amplifier, and display, while toggling it to OFF physically disconnects the battery to eliminate passive power draw and ensure zero current drain when inactive.

Because the ESP32-S3 lacks an internal DAC and only supports BLE 5.0 without Bluetooth Classic A2DP audio streaming, sound relies on the onboard audio pipeline. Digital audio travels directly from the ESP32-S3 to the MAX98357A amplifier on Board B via short I2S traces carrying clock and data signals. To protect screen performance, only the two amplified differential speaker lines cross the board-to-board header to drive the speaker on Board A, preventing high-frequency audio switching noise from interfering with the display's SPI communication lines.

IV. Mechanical Stackup & Clearance Verification
The 15 mm internal standoff gap is derived from the combined height of the internal components and safety margins. Factoring in the thickest internal component—the 8 mm LiPo battery—alongside 4 mm for header pin and component clearances, adding a 3 mm safety air gap completes the 15 mm height requirement. This cushion guarantees that soldered through-hole leads and component edges cannot press into or puncture the LiPo battery pouch, while simultaneously providing sufficient clearance for the USB-C charging port and power switch toggle along the open side profile.
